system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: Deresuscitation

ATOM IVFLUID-C08-S3-03 (S3): De-resuscitation is an active fluid removal to treat fluid accumulation causing organ dysfunction, whereas de-escalation means discontinuing or reducing IV fluids to prevent fluid accumulation.

EVIDENCE:
[IVFLUID-p0515-s09] De-escalation means discontinuation or reducing IV fluids to prevent fluid accumulation.
[IVFLUID-p0515-s10] De-resuscitation is an active fluid removal to treat fluid accumulation causing organ dysfunction.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Joins independently assessable definitions of de-resuscitation and de-escalation. / States two separate definitions (de-resuscitation and de-escalation).
- SCOPE_LABEL: revise — S1: Defines and distinguishes two strategies rather than stating a stopping criterion or applicability limit. / S1: Distinguishing the definition of de-resuscitation from de-escalation belongs in what it is (S1).
- L1_ONLY: hold — The de-escalation clause introduces a second technical concept; separate it from the de-resuscitation definition.
- NO_OVERLAP: hold — Its de-resuscitation definition repeats the active-removal and organ-damage-treatment claim stated more fully in IVFLUID-C08-S1-03.
